headline_marked: Ronaldo scores twice as [[Portugal routs Uzbekistan 5-0]] in Houston
headline: Ronaldo scores twice as Portugal routs Uzbekistan 5-0 in Houston
summary: Cristiano Ronaldo silences critics with a brace, becoming the first player in history to score in six different World Cup editions.
details: Cristiano Ronaldo scored twice in Portugal's 5-0 demolition of Uzbekistan in a Group K clash in Houston, helping his side move to the brink of the knockout stage.

The 41-year-old captain opened the scoring in the sixth minute with a clinical first-time finish and added a second in the 39th minute, slotting past the goalkeeper after a through ball from Bruno Fernandes.
With his first goal, Ronaldo became the first player in history to score in six different World Cup editions (2006, 2010, 2014, 2018, 2022, and 2026), surpassing Lionel Messi's record of five.
At 41 years and 138 days, he became the second-oldest goalscorer in World Cup history, trailing only Roger Milla, and the oldest player ever to score twice in a single World Cup match.
His second goal took him to 10 World Cup goals for Portugal, making him the country's outright leading scorer in the tournament, surpassing Eusebio's tally of nine.
Ronaldo also joined an exclusive club as one of only three players to be both his country's youngest and oldest goalscorer in World Cup history, alongside Michael Laudrup and Lionel Messi.
The performance comes after an underwhelming performance in a 1-1 draw against DR Congo, which had led to questions about his place in the starting eleven.
caption:
6 World Cups, 1 record-breaker. Cristiano Ronaldo just rewrote the history books in Houston!

Cristiano Ronaldo scored twice in Portugal's 5-0 demolition of Uzbekistan in a Group K clash in Houston, helping his side move to the brink of the knockout stage.

The 41-year-old captain opened the scoring in the sixth minute with a clinical first-time finish and added a second in the 39th minute, slotting past the goalkeeper after a through ball from Bruno Fernandes.

With his first goal, Ronaldo became the first player in history to score in six different World Cup editions (2006, 2010, 2014, 2018, 2022, and 2026), surpassing Lionel Messi's record of five.

At 41 years and 138 days, he became the second-oldest goalscorer in World Cup history, trailing only Roger Milla, and the oldest player ever to score twice in a single World Cup match.

His second goal took him to 10 World Cup goals for Portugal, making him the country's outright leading scorer in the tournament, surpassing Eusebio's tally of nine.

Ronaldo also joined an exclusive club as one of only three players to be both his country's youngest and oldest goalscorer in World Cup history, alongside Michael Laudrup and Lionel Messi.

The performance comes after an underwhelming performance in a 1-1 draw against DR Congo, which had led to questions about his place in the starting eleven.

headline_marked: Resolute Ghana [[held England to a 0-0 draw]] in World Cup Group L
headline: Resolute Ghana held England to a 0-0 draw in World Cup Group L
summary: Despite dominating possession, Thomas Tuchel's side failed to break through Ghana's deep defense in their second match of the tournament.
details: England settled for a 0-0 draw against a resolute Ghana side in their second World Cup Group L match on Tuesday.
The Three Lions dominated the game with almost 80% possession in the first half, but were limited to half-chances as Ghana's defense swarmed around Harry Kane and other attackers.
The opening 45 minutes marked the first time in this World Cup where neither side managed a single shot on target.
Ghana's coach Carlos Queiroz, who has extensive experience in English football, drilled the team to defend deep to blunt England's attacking style.
Thomas Tuchel attempted to break the deadlock by introducing Bukayo Saka, Nico O'Reilly, Morgan Rogers, Eberechi Eze, and Marcus Rashford as substitutes.
England missed their best chance of the match in the 86th minute when O'Reilly's header hit the bar and Harry Kane missed the rebound.
The result leaves both teams well-placed to advance to the next phase of the tournament, while Croatia and Panama meet later on Tuesday.
caption:
80% possession, zero shots on target in the first half. England couldn't break Ghana's wall.

England settled for a 0-0 draw against a resolute Ghana side in their second World Cup Group L match on Tuesday.

The Three Lions dominated the game with almost 80% possession in the first half, but were limited to half-chances as Ghana's defense swarmed around Harry Kane and other attackers.

The opening 45 minutes marked the first time in this World Cup where neither side managed a single shot on target.

Ghana's coach Carlos Queiroz, who has extensive experience in English football, drilled the team to defend deep to blunt England's attacking style.

Thomas Tuchel attempted to break the deadlock by introducing Bukayo Saka, Nico O'Reilly, Morgan Rogers, Eberechi Eze, and Marcus Rashford as substitutes.

England missed their best chance of the match in the 86th minute when O'Reilly's header hit the bar and Harry Kane missed the rebound.

The result leaves both teams well-placed to advance to the next phase of the tournament, while Croatia and Panama meet later on Tuesday.
